knowledge:
- key_parameters: Y=Normalized expression matrix with rows representing genes and columns representing samples (e.g., RPKM) ;; GSDB=Gene set database containing pathway definitions (e.g., MSigDB) ;; iES_mat=The calculated iES matrix returned by iES_cal2 ;; cli=Clinical dataset containing survival outcomes (time and status) ;; indVec=Binary vector indicating patient phenotypes, where 0 represents normal/reference samples and 1 represents tumor/test samples ;; gs_str=Character string specifying the pathway/gene set of interest for visualization
- alternatives: Single-gene biomarkers are mentioned as the traditional alternative, but they are limited by variable expression levels and do not capture pathway-level disruption.
- when_to_use: Use when you have transcriptomics data (with both normal/control and tumor/case samples) and clinical survival data, and you want to identify personalized pathway-level biomarkers that predict clinical outcomes.
- pitfalls: Requires a binary phenotype vector (indVec) where normal samples (0) are used as a reference to fit a Gaussian Mixture Model; if normal samples are missing or mislabeled, the classification of perturbed tumor samples will fail. Cox regression in iES_surv may produce convergence warnings if the number of perturbed samples in a pathway is extremely small.

workflows.name: individualized_pathway_analysis
workflows.intent: Calculate personalized pathway enrichment scores (iES) from expression data and test their association with clinical survival outcomes.
input: expression_matrix.csv (normalized gene expression matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns)
gene_set_database.gmt (gene set database containing pathway definitions)
clinical_data.csv (clinical dataset with survival time and status)
phenotype_vector.csv (binary vector indicating normal [0] vs tumor [1] samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the expression matrix, phenotype vector, clinical data, and gene set database ;; 2. Calculate the individualized pathway enrichment score (iES) matrix using iES_cal2 ;; 3. Test the association of iES scores with survival outcomes using iES_surv ;; 4. Visualize the iES distribution and survival differences using water_fall, density_fall, and iES_survPlot
workflows.code:
library(iPath)
data(PRAD_data)
dim(prad_exprs)
data(GSDB_example)
head(prad_cli)
iES_mat = iES_cal2(Y = prad_exprs, GSDB = GSDB_example)
iES_mat[1:2, 1:4]
surv_outcomes = iES_surv(iES_mat = iES_mat, cli = prad_cli, indVec = prad_inds)
head(surv_outcomes)
water_fall(iES_mat, gs_str = "SimPathway2", indVec = prad_inds)
density_fall(iES_mat, gs_str = "SimPathway2", indVec = prad_inds)
iES_survPlot(iES_mat = iES_mat, cli = prad_cli, gs_str = "SimPathway1", indVec = prad_inds, title = TRUE)
